stimulus.title: Phosgene decomposing in a sealed flask
stimulus.html: Phosgene decomposes on heating: COCl2(g) ⇌ CO(g) + Cl2(g). At a certain high temperature, Kc = 8.0 × 10−4. A sealed 1.00 L flask initially contains 0.50 M COCl2 and no CO or Cl2, and is held at that temperature.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the equilibrium concentration of each species in terms of x, where x is the amount of COCl2 that reacts (in M).

accept: an ICE table with these entries

parts.sample: Initial: 0.50, 0, 0. Change: −x, +x, +x. Equilibrium: [COCl<sub>2</sub>] = 0.50 − x, [CO] = x, [Cl<sub>2</sub>] = x.

parts.label: b
parts.sample: K<sub>c</sub> = x<sup>2</sup> / (0.50 − x) = 8.0 × 10<sup>−4</sup>. Because K is small, 0.50 − x ≈ 0.50, so x<sup>2</sup> = (8.0 × 10<sup>−4</sup>)(0.50) = 4.0 × 10<sup>−4</sup> and x = [Cl<sub>2</sub>] = 0.020 M.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Justify the approximation you used in part (b), or explain why none was needed.

rubric.point: x = 0.020 M is 4% of 0.50 M, which is under 5%, so neglecting x in 0.50 − x is justified.

parts.sample: x = 0.020 M is (0.020 / 0.50) × 100% = 4.0% of the initial concentration. That is under 5%, so treating 0.50 − x as 0.50 introduces a negligible error.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Extra CO is injected into the equilibrium mixture at constant temperature. Determine whether [COCl2] increases, decreases or stays the same, and justify your answer in terms of Q and K.

rubric.point: [COCl₂] increases: added CO increases Q = [CO][Cl₂]/[COCl₂] above K, so the net reaction proceeds in reverse, forming COCl₂ until Q = K.

parts.sample: [COCl<sub>2</sub>] increases. Adding CO increases the numerator of Q = [CO][Cl<sub>2</sub>] / [COCl<sub>2</sub>], so Q > K. The net reaction proceeds in reverse, consuming CO and Cl<sub>2</sub> and forming COCl<sub>2</sub>, until Q = K.
